# Judo Kata Tournament Manager

> Browser-based software to organise, score, and display judo kata competitions from one laptop on a local network — draw, judge tablets, live hall results, and printable PDF scoresheets, with no internet required.

Judo Kata Tournament Manager runs an entire judo kata competition from a single
laptop acting as a local server. Judges score on tablets in the browser, organisers
run the draw and manage the field, and the hall shows live results and an announcer
board. It is built for kata organisers, judges, and competition officials. It is
free and open source (AGPL-3.0) and works entirely offline on the venue's local
network — no cloud service and no account.

Full context (llms-full.txt): https://katajudo.com/llms-full.txt

## Key facts

- Free and open source (AGPL-3.0). No subscription, no per-event fee.
- No internet required; runs on a laptop over the venue LAN.
- Optional paid on-site operation and hardware supply are available.
- Supports EJU, kata-judge/BJA-style, and IJF scoring rulesets.
- Live screens in English, French, and German.
- Data is a single SQLite file per event, owned by the organiser.
- Validated against the senior categories of the 2024 Silesian Open Judo Kata Competition.
- No public download yet; demos and supervised test events are open.

## Pricing

- Full pricing: https://katajudo.com/pricing.md
- Software: free (£0, AGPL-3.0).
- On-site support: £100 per day (including travel days), plus accommodation, meals, travel, and any hardware agreed in advance.
- Posted kit: a pre-configured Raspberry Pi, quoted per event.
- Full hardware supply: judge tablets, projector(s), server, and network, quoted on requirements.

## Comparisons

Judo Kata Tournament Manager is free, open-source (AGPL) software that runs an
entire judo kata competition from one laptop on the venue LAN with no internet.
It covers the draw, named judge tablets, live hall results, the announcer board,
printable PDF packs, and CSV exports, and supports EJU, kata-judge/BJA-style, and
IJF rulesets.

- Judo Kata Judge (https://kata-judge.judowaza.org/) is an open-source (AGPL)
  IJF-ruleset kata judging web app that stores data in Azure Cosmos DB (cloud).
- Michel Kozlowski's Excel "Kata Scoresheets (EJU)"
  (https://sites.google.com/site/katascoresheets/) is the spreadsheet many EJU
  organisers use; this project follows it and is dedicated to his memory.

## Scoring

Choose one ruleset in Config; the same tablet marks produce the event total.
- EJU: drops highest and lowest judge totals with three or more judges; a forgotten technique zeroes that technique and halves that judge's total once, rounded up.
- kata-judge/BJA-style: discards per technique; scores stay between 1 and 10; halves without rounding up.
- IJF: discards per technique; five judges drop high and low, four drop low, three or fewer keep every mark; a forgotten mark halves the pair total once.
- Tie-breaks: fewer big mistakes, then medium, then small, then average score.
- Shadow judge seats are stored but never counted.

## Supported kata

Nage-no-Kata (including 1G, 2G, 3G, 3-set), Katame-no-Kata (including 1G),
Ju-no-Kata, Kime-no-Kata, Kodokan Goshin Jutsu, Koshiki-no-Kata,
Itsutsu-no-Kata, and Kodomo-no-Kata 1–7.
